chapter: Chicago, the Marable boats and Marge's St. Louis family band
title: First regular Chicago job; Marge's jealousy and manicuring
summary: Marge recalls Zutty's first Chicago job, her jealousy and her work as a manicurist in a friend's shop, which kept them going for months during the three-month union wait.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Do you remember your first job, first regular job you had in Chicago?
That was a first job because that's when I quit playing. I quit before I even made a week's pay.
Yeah.
What do you mean, that was the first job in Chicago?
First regular job in Chicago.
Oh, oh. Well, we're starting at a good point.
I had worked for Baby Dodds, Baby Dodds laid off one night and he wanted to --
Yeah, but you were saying that was your first job.
Yes.

I know that was your first job because, boy, he was so hurt because I had to play with this other band and everything, and he was so jealous and (inaudible). Life was miserable, really. (Inaudible) this other band.
Oh.

He said he knew musicians and he how they were AFTER me... (unintelligible). Soon as he said he was going to work with Vernon Roulette (unintelligible). Oh, yeah, and then I had another job. I quit the day -- I was working as a manicurist. Zutty was jealous of that job. He said (unintelligible). He said he going to work with Vernon Roulette was (unintelligible) I told the barber shop man I wouldn't be to work no more. Finished.
Yeah.
And I hadn't played or you know and -- well, I've worked since.
Marge used to hurt those cats working on those nails so badly. I used to watch them flinch because I'd meet him, I'd meet Marge every day.
Every night.
Every night I was there waiting for her.
His friend from New Orleans owned the shop.
Willie Beasley.
Well, Marge had you had experience doing it?
I had taken a course at Madame Malone's in St. Louis, but had never worked at it.
Oh.
I tell you, I was in hardly everything.
I suppose doing that is sort of just
a matter of doing it, really.
Yeah.
Practice.
Murge used to hurt some poor guy (inaudible).
It kept us going for almost six months.
Yeah.
Because we weren't doing a thing. And as soon as he said he had this job, the union had okayed he could work, that's it.
How long did you have to wait before you could go out?
Three months.
Three months.
Oh, yes, I see.
But even after he was able to work why he couldn't get any. He didn't get a job right away. This job --
Running a little gig, you know.
Yeah, but he couldn't get a regular job. He didn't get a regular job. We were hired and that was it.
